intro: Your record shop, Hollow Records, closed in 2019. Three local covers nobody bought are still behind the counter: 'Lose Yourself', 'Sweet Child O' Mine' and 'Despacito'. Your old flip phone buzzes. Press Q to open it.

travelLines.present: Snap. The phone closes and it's today again.

notHereLine: There's nothing to use here right now.
ending: Three forgotten CDs, one famous shop. Something old, into something modern. Press Enter to play again.

reputation.label: Hollow Records is open again
reputation.line: The boards are gone. The lights are on, there's music inside, and someone is already flicking through the racks.

offline.headline: Hollow Records Reopens Its Doors
offline.article: The corner record shop that closed in 2004 is open again. Locals say it all started with one forgotten CD.

reputation.label: the shop is busy every weekend
reputation.line: There are posters in the window and a queue out of the door.

offline.headline: Weekend Queues at Hollow Records
offline.article: Two of the shop's forgotten 2004 CDs are now cult favourites. Fans travel across London to buy them where it all began.

reputation.label: the shop is a London landmark
reputation.line: A blue plaque by the door: 'Where the 2004 sound was discovered.'

offline.headline: Blue Plaque for the Shop That Found the 2004 Sound
offline.article: Three artists nobody had heard of in 2004 are now household names. All three were first championed by one small record shop on this corner.

news.unchangedFact: Hollow Records, the record shop on the corner, closed in 2019 and has been boarded up ever since.

default.headline: Corner Shop Still Boarded Up, Seven Years On
default.article: Hollow Records closed its doors in 2019 and nobody has opened them since. Neighbours say the street has been quieter without the music.
